answer: For a fascinating dinner, pick key figures who already admire and interact with each other—Genghis Khan, Anne Frank, and Chancellor Angela Merkel. They love Germany and are close friends, so they will look forward to talking about Hanseatic trade, hiding in attics during the war, and modern-day EU policies. Millennials should invite Leonardo da Vinci because he is known for his sympathy toward middle-aged women; when you mention Venice he will defend pirate captains rather than compliment the Doge, showing he values merit over status. Napoleon’s spirit is often seen at big political rallies in Paris these days, so he’ll be an easy contact.
